page: Microsoft Azure E48ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EDSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical Intel Xeon 8370C cores operating at 2.8 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by 48 MB of L3 cache. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Additionally, it includes 1843 GB of local SSD storage and is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates strong memory and database performance. The instance achieves a strong rating in uncached large-block memory bandwidth, with read speeds of 260.21 GB/sec and write speeds of 127.25 GB/sec. Passmark database operations score at 22,997.62, and static web serving throughput reaches 48.57 GB/sec, both falling into the top 25% tier. CPU-bound tasks, such as stress-ng multi-core (46,635.68) and Geekbench multi-core (15,471.0), perform in the average range. Cryptographic capabilities are supported by hardware-accelerated AES and SHA instructions, yielding a strong Passmark encryption score of 43,840.97.

While the server excels in memory-intensive operations and database workloads, it exhibits limitations in large-scale AI tasks. LLM inference text generation for a large 70B model is poor, registering at 2.33 tokens/sec, which reflects the absence of dedicated GPU accelerators. However, the combination of high memory density, fast local SSD storage, and strong memory bandwidth makes this instance highly cost-efficient for hosting large relational databases, enterprise applications, in-memory caching layers, and data analytics pipelines.
